hints: Look closely at the combination of clues, especially being incredibly flexible and more conductive than copper at the same time.
Remember that diamond is hard but brittle and does not conduct, while graphite is slippery and conductive but is made of many stacked layers.
Think about which single-atom-thick sheet of carbon is famous for being light, super strong, flexible and an excellent conductor.
walkthrough:
**Decode the Clues in the Quote**

Think like a detective. Lighter than a feather suggests extremely thin and low density. Stronger than steel yet flexible rules out anything brittle. More conductive than copper means it must have mobile electrons.

Key idea: we need strong + flexible + conducting.

**Recall the Carbon Allotropes**

All four options are pure carbon, just arranged differently. Diamond is a 3D tetrahedral network, very hard but brittle and non-conducting. Graphite is stacked layers, slippery and conducting. Buckminsterfullerene is closed $\text{C}_{60}$ cages. Graphene is a single hexagonal sheet.

Structure: $$\text{graphene = one layer of sp}^2 \text{ carbon in hexagons}$$

**Match Properties to Structure**

Only a single layer can be both almost weightless and transparent yet immensely strong in the plane. Its delocalised pi electrons move freely across the sheet, giving superb electrical conductivity and flexibility.

Conclusion: the description fits the wonder material, graphene.

options.A: Buckminsterfullerene, $\text{C}_{60}$, is made of closed ball-like cages. It is interesting for nanotechnology but it is not described as stronger than steel, flexible sheets, or better than copper at conducting.
options.B: Diamond is very hard because every carbon is tetrahedrally bonded in 3D, but it is brittle, not flexible, and it is an electrical insulator with no mobile electrons. It cannot be more conductive than copper.
options.C: Graphene is a single layer of graphite, one atom thick. It is extremely light, about 200 times stronger than steel by weight, flexible, transparent, and an excellent electrical conductor due to delocalised electrons. This matches all four clues perfectly.
options.D: Graphite does conduct electricity and is soft and slippery, but it is a bulk 3D stack of many layers held by weak forces. It is not described as lighter than a feather, super strong, or incredibly flexible like an isolated single sheet.
